sources.text: Search this site Embedded Files Grassian Group at UCSD The Grassian re search group focuses on the chemistry and impacts of environmental interfaces including atmospheric aerosols, aqueous microdroplets, engineered and geochemical nanomaterials, and indoor surfaces. Group Meeting Schedule: Click here for the schedule . Support Our Students Please Donate: WELCOME TO THE GRASSIAN GROUP WEBSITE! This website provides an overview of the research explored in the Environmental Interfaces Laboratory, located on the University of California San Diego campus. Broadly, research in the Grassian group centers on molecular-level laboratory studies aimed at advancing our understanding of the chemistry and global impacts of environmental interfaces. Environmental interfaces are broadly defined as any surface in equilibrium/contact with its surrounding environment or any environmental system were the surface plays an important role. Current projects span a range of topics, including the heterogeneous chemistry of trace gases—both organic and inorganic—with atmospheric particulate matter and urban surfaces such as mineral dust, sea spray, and indoor surfaces; chemistry within aqueous microdroplets and at the air/water interface; the dissolution, mobilization, and multiphase chemistry of iron-containing particles; sulfur oxidation in aqueous aerosols; multiphase photochemistry of nitrogen oxides, particularly pathways leading to HONO formation in both indoor and outdoor environments; surface chemistry and interactions of biological macromolecules with geochemical nanoparticles; links between particulate matter and human health; and the environmental and health-related applications and implications of nanoscience and nanotechnology. If you have questions about our research as you explore the site, please feel free to contact any of our group members.
